Instant appeal has been filed by the appellants-defendants (for short 'the defendants') against the judgment and decree dated 06.05.2009 passed by Additional District Judge (Fast Track) No.5,
Jaipur City, Jaipur in Civil Suit No.36/2006 (478/2003), whereby the trial court decreed the respondents-plaintiffs' (for short 'the plaintiffs') suit for possession, mesne profit and permanent injunction.

sentences.text:
Brief facts of the case are that the plaintiffs filed a suit for possession, mesne profit and permanent injunction against the defendant alleging that property situated at Dundlod House Hawa Sarak,
Jaipur was partitioned between the plaintiff No.1 and defendant by virtue of family settlement.

Satish Dabi who is power of attorney of the defendant, sold the disputed property to the plaintiff vide two different sale deeds dated 07.12.2000 and registry of half of the portion was done on 20.12.2000 for a sale consideration of Rs.4 lac.
Defendant requested the plaintiffs and sought sometime to vacate the possession of the disputed property but he had not handed over the possession.
Hence the suit was filed by the plaintiff.

Defendant filed his written statement and stated that he had executed an agreement to sell dated 08.09.2000 in favour of Satish Dabi to sell the disputed property in question for sale consideration of Rs.42,00,000/-.
As per the terms of agreement, Satish Dabi paid Rs.5 lacs in cash and rest of the amount was to be paid till 20.10.2000.
Satish Dabi failed to pay the balance amount.
So, agreement to sell stood cancelled.
Property in question was mortgaged with Rajasthan Financial Corporation.
So, defendant wanted to settle the loan amount.

On 16.11.2000, (3 of 12) [CFA-401/2009] Satish Dabi further offered Rs.2 lacs in cash and a cheque of Rs.13 lacs to the defendant and assured to pay the balance amount of sale consideration till December, 2000.
Thereafter, on the contention of Satish Dabi, the defendant further executed a power of attorney on 16.11.2000 in favour of Satish Dabi.
Satish Dabi failed to fulfill the commitment.
So, by way of public notice on 27.02.2001 the defendant declared the power of attorney cancelled and also sent the legal notice dated 15.08.2001 to Satish Dabi.

On 17.10.2001, the defendant received a letter from plaintiff and immediately thereafter, the defendant filed a civil suit before the Competent Court bearing Civil Suit No.135/2004 for declaration and permanent injunction.
Defendant also lodged FIR against Satish Dabi, plaintiffs and their sons for the offence under Sections 420, 465, 467, 468, 471 and 120B IPC.

It was further mentioned that the defendant and plaintiff No.1 obtained a loan from Rajasthan Thakur Ranveer Singh S/O Shri Harnath ... vs Rajveer Singh S/O Shri Harnath Sing on 19 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24305408/
2
Financial Corporation for development of their joint property of Dundlod Castle, situated at Jhunjhunu.
They failed to repay the loan, therefore the RFC took symbolic possession of the property in question.
So, suit filed by the plaintiffs be dismissed.

On the basis of the pleading of the parties, learned trial court framed the following issues:-
(1) Whether plaintiff Nos.1 and 2 had purchased the undivided land and house mentioned in para No.1 of plaint from the defendant by way of two different sale deeds dated 07.12.2000 and plaintiffs are the owners of purchased property?

(2)
Whether plaintiffs are entitled to get possession of suit property from defendant?
(4 of 12) [CFA-401/2009] (3) Whether plaintiffs are entitled to get Rs.30,000/- as mesne profit till filing of suit and further entitled to get Rs.10,000/- per month mesne profit till getting possession from the defendant?
(4) Whether plaintiffs are entitled to get the defendant bound down from permanent injunction?

(5) Whether defendant had not executed power of attorney dated 16.11.2000 in favour of Satish Dabi for selling his property but executed the same for selling him property and that was cancelled prior to selling the property to the plaintiffs?

(6) Whether defendant is not bound by the sale deed dated 07.12.2000 executed in favour of plaintiff Nos.1 and 2? (7) Relief?
Learned counsel for the defendant submits that the trial court passed the judgment and decree against the defendant in a cursory manner and had not appreciated the evidence led by the parties in right perspective.

Learned counsel for the defendant also submits that it is an admitted position that property in question was mortgaged with the RFC and original title deed of the property was under possession of the RFC.

So, plaintiffs were very well aware about this fact that property could not be sold or transfered prior to satisfying the loan of RFC but to obtain wrongful gain from the defendant, the plaintiff-Rajveer Singh hatched a conspiracy with Satish Dabi who was power of attorney holder of the defendant and got the sale deeds registered, which are ab-initio void.

Learned counsel for the defendant also submits that the defendant-Thakur Ranveer Singh entered into an agreement to sell the disputed property with Satish Dabi on 08.09.2000 for sale (5 of 12)
[CFA-401/2009] consideration of Rs.42 lacs for settling the dues of RFC but Satish Dabi did not fulfil the terms and conditions of so-called agreement.

After that, defendant executed power of attorney in favour of Satish Dabi on 16.11.2000 for settling the dues of RFC but Satish Dabi wrongly executed sale deed in favour of plaintiffs without giving entire sale consideration of Rs.42 lacs to the defendant.
Learned counsel for the defendant also submits that during evidence, affidavit of Satish Dabi was submitted by the plaintiffs but they did not produce him in the evidence.
So, defendant failed to confront him.
So, it is an admitted position that Satish Dabi had played the mischief with the defendant.
Defendant had lodged FIR against Satish Dabi and plaintiffs and their sons.

The defendant filed S.B.
Civil First Appeal No.418/2007 in which this court directed to maintain status quo regarding property in question.
After that, defendant also filed an application before the trial court for staying the suit proceeding but trial court dismissed the application filed by the defendant.
Defendant challenged the said order by writ petition No.4464/2008 before this Court and procured stay order in his favour but the said writ petition was dismissed in default on 20.10.2008.
Defendant filed an application before the trial court for staying proceedings till restoration but trial court turned down the request and passed the impugned decree in hasty manner.

Learned counsel for the defendant also submits that defendant filed an application before the trial court under Order 11 Rule 12 and 14 CPC for producing mortgaged document in which defendant as well as plaintiff signed the agreement for procuring the loan but the trial court rejected the said application without any cogent reason.

Learned counsel for the defendant also submits that the defendant had also filed an application before the trial court under Order 14 Rule 5 CPC for framing of additional issue but the said application was also dismissed while passing the impugned judgment and decree.

Learned counsel for the defendant also submits that the trial court while passing the impugned judgment and decree observed that it would be subject to outcome of appeal No.418/2007 pending before this Court.
Learned counsel for the defendant also submits that the trial court had assumed that pending appeal would be dismissed.
Learned counsel for the defendant also submits that defendant had withdrawn S.B. Civil First Appeal No.418/2007 with liberty to file fresh suit for cancellation of sale deed.
So, present appeal is maintainable.
Learned counsel for the defendant also submits that plaintiff-Uma Kumari had challenged the auction proceedings but the petition filed by Uma Kumari was dismissed.

Learned counsel for the defendant also submits that as per sale deeds (Ex.2 and Ex.6), possession was handed over to plaintiff-Rajveer Singh but Rajveer Singh wrote a letter to the defendant-Thakur Ranveer Singh on 22.09.2001 (Ex.22) in which he demanded the possession.
So, it is contrary to the sale deed.

sentences.text: I have considered the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the defendant as well as learned counsel for the plaintiffs.
It is an admitted position that disputed property was mortgaged with RFC and original documents were in possession of RFC.
Plaintiff who is brother of defendant-Thakur Ranveer Singh also well aware of this fact that property could not be sold or (11 of 12) [CFA-401/2009] transferred prior to satisfying the loan of RFC.

Defendant by way of evidence clearly proved execution of agreement Thakur Ranveer Singh S/O Shri Harnath ... vs Rajveer Singh S/O Shri Harnath Sing on 19 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24305408/
6 dated 08.09.2000
by which defendant wanted to sell the disputed property on sale consideration of Rs.42 lacs for settling the dues of RFC.
Agreement dated 08.09.2000 was executed in favour of Satish Dabi but Satish Dabi did not fulfill the terms and conditions of the agreement.

After that,
defendant executed the power of attorney on 16.11.2000 in continuation of the agreement dated 08.09.2000.
Satish Dabi had paid Rs.26 lacs out of Rs.42 lacs for settling the dues of the RFC to defendant Thakur Ranveer Singh.
Receipts exhibited by defendant clearly shows these transaction.
Agreement dated 08.09.2000 was mentioned in receipts (Ex.10 to Ex.18).

It is well established fact that plaintiff who is brother of the defendant had given evasive reply in cross-examination that he had not enquired about so-called agreement dated 08.09.2000 mentioned in these receipts from Thakur Ranveer Singh.
Plaintiff Uma Kumari had challenged the auction proceedings.
So, Rajveer Singh and Uma Kumari very well knew that these properties were mortgaged with RFC and without clearance of loan, the property could not be transferred.

As per sale deed (Ex.2 and Ex.6),
possession was handed over but plaintiff Rajveer Singh had written letter to defendant Thakur Ranveer Singh for giving possession.
The said letter was exhibited as Ex.22.
It is contrary to the possession given mentioned in the sale deeds.
A perusal of the sale deed (Ex.2 and Ex.6) revealed that payment of Rs.26 lacs was made and Rs.1 lac would be paid later on was not mentioned in it.
Payment receipts which were exhibited by the plaintiffs were not proved because plaintiffs failed to adduce evidence of Satish (12 of 12) [CFA-401/2009] Dabi.
If the plaintiffs adduced the evidence of Satish Dabi during the trial then position would have been cleared.
These receipts revealed payment by Satish Dabi to Thakur Ranveer Singh not by the Rajveer Singh.
Trial court had committed error in passing the decree in favour of the plaintiff subject to decision of appeal pending before this Court.
The trial court virtually assumed that appeal would be dismissed.
So, in my considered opinion, the present appeal deserves to be allowed.
Defendant as well as plaintiffs both have submitted the applications under Order 41 Rule 27 CPC for taking certain documents on record.
This Court at that time ordered to consider these applications at the time of final hearing.
A bare perusal of these applications revealed that documents filed by both the parties are not relevant to adjudicate this appeal.
So, both the applications are liable to be dismissed.

Defendant had also filed an application under Order 1 Rule 10 CPC to implead the RFC as a party on account of property mortgaged with RFC but in my considered opinion, present appeal can be adjudicated without impleading RFC as a party.
So, application filed by the defendant also liable to be dismissed, which stands dismissed.
The Civil First Appeal filed by the defendant is allowed.
The judgment and decree dated 06.05.2009 passed by the trial court is set aside.
Pending application(s), if any, stand(s) disposed of.
